To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new design procedure for mechanical sleeves in surface mounted high speed PM synchronous machines has been proposed and validated.
the proposed approach can be effectively used to design the PM retention sleeve for HS-PMSMs.
“The proposed procedure can be used for fast and effective design of HS-PMSM with different PMs and/or sleeve materials”.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an analytical procedure that allows the design of HS-PMSMs, with particular regard to the rotor structure.

the following aspects: (i) the design of the mechanical sleeve; (ii) the analysis of the stress and strain distributions in the sleeve, in the PMs and in the shaft; (iii) the analysis of PM demagnetization phenomena.
the development of a design methodology that can be used for the design of HS-PMSMs with different PM materials, rotor structures and sleeve materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed procedure can be successfully employed for the fast design of HS-PMSMs, as well as for the evaluation of the mechanical stress and contact pressure between PMs and sleeve.

the proposed procedure is able to predict the contact pressure and the Von Mise stress in the sleeve, with a maximum relative deviation of 5% and 8% from the results provided by the Finite Element Method (FEM), respectively.
the proposed analytical approach can be used to design HS-PMSMs with different materials, and it can be easily integrated in an automated design procedure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed procedure allows for a fast, accurate and effective HS-PM machine design, which is of particular importance for the development of High-Temperature-Superconducting (HTS) PM machines.
the analytical approach is able to predict the stress and contact pressure distribution along the rotor with an accuracy comparable with FEA.
, the proposed procedure can be used to design HS-PMSM with different PMs and sleeve materials, and the FEA is used to validate the analytical approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the employment of Titanium sleeves is preferable in terms of contact pressures, Von Mises equivalent stresses, as well as PMs demagnetization.
, by employing a Titanium sleeve, it is possible to increase the maximum speed of the machine up to about 60% compared to a standard HS-PMSM.
the proposed design approach allows the computation of contact forces between rotor layers, which can be used to estimate the maximum torque and to evaluate the maximum temperature rise in the rotor.
